newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: ACCC sees problems in any NAB St George bid.
newsitem.headline: ACCC sees problems in any NAB St George bid.

text.p: Australia's anti-monopolies authority, the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission (ACCC), said on Friday it saw significant problems in granting approval for any potential bid for St George Bank Ltd by a major Australian bank.

Asked what implications the approval of the Westpac Banking Corp -Bank of Melbourne merger had for a possible National Australia Bank Ltd bid for St George, ACCC chairman Alan Fels said: "There are some fairly significant differences which we would have to look at closely."

National Australia Bank (NAB) has been suggested as a possible bidder for St George, Australia's fifth largest retail bank, after the Australian government ruled out mergers between the big four Australian banks.
The major four banks are NAB, Westpac, Commonwealth Bank of Australia and the Australia and New Zealand Banking Group Ltd.
